tasks.title: Capture the Hermes TUI reference contract
acceptance: Record the reference build, environment, terminal size, and capture method.
Capture startup, input, navigation, error, and exit observations without redacting behavior into guesses.
Mark every unobserved behavior as unknown and link the resulting ledger entries.

result.summary: Pinned Hermes TUI reference behavior captured at 120x40 with sanitized startup frame and lifecycle trace; unknown behavior is explicitly listed.

tasks.title: Define the first replay trace and golden-frame fixtures
acceptance: Add one sanitized reference trace with ordered inputs and observable outputs.
Add the matching normalized terminal frame fixture.
Document normalization rules so unrelated terminal noise cannot hide a regression.

result.summary: Added the sanitized ordered lifecycle trace, normalized 120x40 startup frame, and explicit normalization contract.

tasks.title: Characterize startup and exit lifecycle parity
acceptance: Define observable startup and exit states for the chosen reference build.
Define behavior for normal exit, interrupt exit, and terminal cleanup.
Add a deterministic probe that fails if cleanup is skipped.

result.summary: Added and wired a real-PTY lifecycle oracle covering startup, raw mode, resize, normal exit, interrupt exit, alternate-screen/cursor cleanup, and termios restoration; just verify passes.

tasks.title: Implement the first reference-backed state transition
acceptance: Implement only behavior covered by the first trace.
Keep the transition deterministic and independent of terminal rendering.
Prove the transition with a focused regression test and replay evidence.

result.summary: Implemented the first trace-backed submit -> busy -> Ctrl+C interrupt transition with typed core state, focused reducer tests, a sanitized replay fixture, and a passing PTY integration oracle.

tasks.title: Implement the first golden-frame-backed visual surface
acceptance: Render the reference-backed surface at the captured terminal size.
Compare normalized cells rather than a human eyeball check.
Record intentional terminal-dependent differences explicitly.

result.summary: Implemented the normalized Hermes startup surface at 120x40 with a product-owned Ratatui asset, cell-level golden comparison, dynamic input/busy assertions, and documented terminal-dependent differences.

tasks.title: Build the differential replay verification command
acceptance: Replay a sanitized trace against Hades and emit a machine-readable result.
Fail on behavioral or visual divergence with the first useful diff.
Keep reference artifacts and generated reports separate.

result.summary: Added a machine-readable differential replay command that compares the normalized 120x40 Hermes golden frame, replays the sanitized submit/interrupt trace in a PTY, reports first-cell visual diffs, and verifies terminal cleanup; wired it into just replay-differential and the full verification gate.

tasks.title: Match the observed busy and interrupted visual states
acceptance: Render the observed musing/mulling busy markers and interrupt affordance at 120x40.
Render an interrupted ready state with the observed completion marker without changing the core transition contract.
Add executable visual/replay assertions and document normalization boundaries and intentional differences.

result.summary: Aligned the 120x40 busy and interrupted projection with the observed Hermes markers, added the OBS-0006 normalized visual contract, and made differential replay consume the contract while preserving the typed core transition.

tasks.title: Implement the observed Ctrl+X session switcher overlay
acceptance: Open a deterministic Sessions overlay from ready state with Ctrl+X.
Expose the observed current/live/resumable/new and keyboard-control landmarks at 120x40.
Close the modal with Esc and prove that composer input resumes without changing unobserved session semantics.

result.summary: Implemented typed Sessions overlay state with Ctrl+X open and Esc close behavior, added the normalized 120x40 overlay projection and contract fixture, and extended differential replay to prove modal landmarks, post-close composer input, and terminal cleanup.

tasks.title: Implement the observed setup-required overlay path
acceptance: Keep /help in the composer and open a Setup Required overlay with the observed provider message and actions.
Clear the retained input on the first Ctrl+C while keeping the setup overlay visible.
Exit cleanly on the second Ctrl+C and document that provider setup/model behavior remains unimplemented.

result.summary: Implemented the observed provider-missing /help path with retained input, a Setup Required overlay, first-Ctrl+C input clearing, second-Ctrl+C clean exit, and contract-driven PTY replay coverage while leaving provider setup unimplemented.

tasks.title: Capture the extended Hermes editing and keymap contract
acceptance: Capture deterministic reference behavior for history navigation, multiline or editing keys, and slash completion where the pinned Hermes runtime exposes it.
Record environment-sensitive interactions such as Ctrl+G, paste, and mouse as observed, unavailable, or unknown without filling gaps with guesses.
Add a sanitized trace and provenance document that preserves exact input bytes, terminal dimensions, normalization, and the reference commit.

result.summary: Captured the pinned Hermes input-editing and keymap contract with fresh synthetic PTY probes: history recall, cursor editing, multiline fallback, slash completion, Ctrl+G editor return, bracketed paste, and the empty-clipboard miss path. Added exact input-byte provenance, explicit environment-sensitive unknowns, a sanitized fixture validator, and wired it into the required verification gate.

tasks.title: Implement the reference-backed composer editing core
acceptance: Add a dedicated cursor-aware composer model covering the observed Left, Backspace, Home, End, Ctrl+A, and Ctrl+K editing behavior without relying on byte-invalid String slicing.
Record successful submitted drafts in session-local history and implement Up/Down recall with the observed newest-entry-to-empty-draft behavior; do not claim restart persistence.
Implement the observed backslash-plus-Enter multiline fallback without submitting, render the resulting draft, and prove the slice with deterministic reducer, snapshot, and PTY replay evidence.

result.summary: Implemented the reference-backed Unicode-safe composer editing core with cursor movement, history recall, multiline fallback, terminal key translation, TUI rendering, and isolated tmux screen replay evidence.

tasks.title: Implement the reference-backed slash completion slice
acceptance: Represent ready-state slash completion as typed state with the exact observed /he items: /help, /hermes-agent, and /hermes-agent-skill-authoring.
Apply completion with Tab to /help, collapse the panel, and leave unobserved completion contexts, ordering, and debounce races explicitly unclaimed.
Render the completion panel and prove typing and application with deterministic tests, a 120x40 snapshot, and isolated PTY replay integrated into verification.

result.summary: Implemented the narrow reference-backed /he slash-completion slice with typed completion state, deterministic panel rendering, Tab application of /help before surface navigation, focused tests, and isolated tmux screen replay integrated into verification.

tasks.title: Implement the observed bracketed paste path
acceptance: Accept a bracketed paste event in the ready composer, preserve embedded newlines at the cursor, and never submit the pasted draft as a side effect.
Wire the terminal paste event into the reducer and render the preserved multiline draft without claiming clipboard-provider or busy-state behavior.
Prove the path with deterministic core/app tests, a 120x40 snapshot, and isolated PTY replay integrated into the full verification gate.

result.summary: Implemented the observed bracketed-paste path with typed crossterm paste events, cursor insertion preserving embedded newlines without submission, TUI rendering, focused tests, and isolated tmux replay integrated into verification.

tasks.title: Implement the observed unchanged-draft editor handoff
acceptance: Emit a typed editor-request outcome for Ctrl+G from a ready non-empty composer instead of silently ignoring the key.
Suspend the alternate screen and raw mode, invoke the configured EDITOR against a temporary draft, and resubmit the unchanged draft after a clean editor exit while restoring terminal state.

Prove the EDITOR=/bin/true unchanged-draft path with reducer tests, terminal cleanup evidence, and isolated PTY replay; leave modified, cancelled, multiline, and unavailable-editor behavior explicitly unclaimed.

result.summary: Implemented the observed unchanged-draft Ctrl+G editor handoff with a typed editor request, temporary draft file, raw/alternate-screen suspension and restoration, configured EDITOR invocation, busy submission, focused reducer coverage, and isolated tmux replay.

tasks.title: Implement the observed empty-clipboard fallback
acceptance: Handle Ctrl+V in the ready composer when no readable clipboard provider is available by reporting No image found in clipboard and leaving the draft unchanged.
Render the observed miss message in the 120x40 Hermes surface without claiming successful text, image, or path clipboard reads.
Prove the path with reducer and snapshot tests plus an isolated PTY replay integrated into the full verification gate.

result.summary: Implemented the observed empty-clipboard Ctrl+V fallback with the exact miss message, unchanged draft semantics, 120x40 rendering, focused tests, and isolated tmux replay integrated into verification.

tasks.title: Capture persistent Hermes input history parity
acceptance: Use the pinned Hermes reference with a fresh synthetic HERMES_HOME to seed a uniquely identifiable submission, then start a second process against the same home and verify Up/Down recall across the process boundary.

Probe the reference-defined persistence edges that are safe and deterministic: consecutive duplicate suppression, trimming behavior, and a multiline entry's on-disk encoding; preserve exact bytes, terminal dimensions, runtime, and source commit.

Add a sanitized provenance document and machine-validated fixture, update the parity matrix and fixture documentation, and leave any unobservable edge explicitly unknown without implementing Hades behavior in this research task.

result.summary: Captured pinned Hermes persistent input-history parity across process restart, consecutive duplicates, multiline + encoding, and the 1,000-entry load cap; added a sanitized fixture, provenance record, matrix/docs updates, validator integration, and a green full verification gate.

tasks.title: Implement persistent input history parity
acceptance: Load and persist ordinary submitted drafts through HERMES_HOME/.hermes_history, falling back to HOME/.hermes/.hermes_history when HERMES_HOME is unset, while keeping startup and write failures non-fatal.

Match the observed Hermes semantics: trim outer whitespace, suppress only a consecutive newest duplicate, preserve multiline entries as + records, and navigate only the newest 1,000 loaded entries without breaking the existing in-process Up/Down draft behavior.

Keep the core reducer deterministic through injected history state and prove the storage/parser rules with focused tests plus a real two-process PTY replay covering restart recall, duplicate byte stability, multiline readback, and the 1,000-entry load cap.

Update the Hades implementation contract, provenance note, parity matrix, replay command, fixture documentation, and full verification gate; do not claim history clearing, malformed-file recovery, concurrent writers, or session recovery.

result.summary: Implemented Hermes-compatible persistent input history with deterministic core injection, fail-open disk storage, restart recall, duplicate suppression, multiline records, newest-1000 cap, isolated PTY replay, and verification-gate integration.

tasks.title: Capture Hermes editor modified and cancelled draft parity
acceptance: Use the pinned Hermes reference and controlled editor commands to capture clean exit with modified content, multiline content, empty output, and nonzero cancellation from Ctrl+G.
Record whether the original composer is cleared, preserved, or submitted for each outcome, including exact trimming and multiline preservation visible at the TUI boundary.

Add a sanitized provenance observation and machine-validated fixture linked to the existing editor contract, update the parity matrix and fixture documentation, and leave unavailable-editor and interactive-editor edge cases explicitly unknown.
Keep this task research-only: do not change Hades implementation behavior until the reference contract is stable and reviewable.

result.summary: Captured deterministic Hermes editor outcomes on the pinned 0.19.1 reference: modified and multiline clean exits submit trimmed text, trailing-newline trimming preserves meaningful spaces, empty output preserves the draft, and nonzero exit cancels without submission; added provenance, validated fixture, and gate/docs links.

tasks.title: Implement deterministic editor outcome parity
acceptance: Match OBS-0018 for configured Ctrl+G editor commands: a clean non-empty exit submits the edited draft, preserves internal newlines, and removes only trailing whitespace from the final result.
Treat clean empty editor output and nonzero editor exit as cancellation: preserve the original composer draft, avoid submission, and restore the TUI cleanly.
Keep ordinary Enter submission semantics intact while adding focused reducer/storage tests for editor-specific trimEnd behavior, multiline history encoding, empty output, and cancellation.

Add a sanitized Hades implementation contract and isolated PTY replay derived from OBS-0018, wire it into just verify, update the implementation contract and parity matrix, and do not claim interactive-editor, unavailable-editor, or busy-turn behavior.

result.summary: Implemented deterministic Hermes editor outcome parity: tokenized VISUAL/EDITOR execution, trimEnd-based non-empty editor submission with multiline preservation, empty-output draft retention, nonzero cancellation, history-compatible normalization, focused tests, and a five-case isolated PTY replay.

tasks.title: Capture Hermes native modified Enter parity
acceptance: Use the pinned Hermes reference with a direct PTY byte stream, not tmux key translation, to send the documented Shift+Enter and Alt+Enter CSI-u sequences.
Record whether each modified Enter inserts a newline without submitting, including exact input bytes, composer text, ready/busy state, and a normal Enter control case.

Add a sanitized provenance observation and machine-validated fixture, update the prior keymap unknowns, fixture documentation, parity matrix, and verification gate without claiming unsupported terminal emulator behavior.
Keep this task research-only: do not change Hades input mapping until the reference bytes and post-input state are stable and reviewable.

result.summary: Captured the pinned Hermes native modified-Enter contract through a direct 120x40 PTY: CSI-u Shift+Enter and Alt+Enter insert a newline without submission, while plain Enter submits; alternate terminal encodings and universal terminal support remain unknown.

tasks.title: Implement native modified Enter parity
acceptance: Map terminal Enter events carrying Shift or Alt modifiers to composer newline insertion without submission, matching the stable CSI-u Shift+Enter and Alt+Enter contract from OBS-0020.
Keep ordinary Enter submission unchanged and add focused core, application, and CLI tests proving modified cases remain ready with multiline composer content while plain Enter enters busy state.
Add a sanitized Hades implementation contract and direct-PTY replay derived from OBS-0020, wire the replay into just verify, and update the parity matrix and fixture documentation.
Do not claim xterm modifyOtherKeys, Ctrl+Enter, or universal terminal-emulator support; this task covers only modifier events actually decoded by the Hades input layer.

result.summary: Implemented the stable modified-Enter slice: crossterm CSI-u Enter events with Shift or Alt map to a typed newline insertion, ordinary Enter still submits, focused core/app/CLI tests cover both paths, and a direct 120x40 PTY replay passes Shift+Enter, Alt+Enter, and plain Enter controls without claiming alternate encodings.

tasks.title: Capture Hermes successful text clipboard parity
acceptance: Use the pinned Hermes reference in a direct 120x40 PTY with a synthetic clipboard provider, not the host clipboard, to capture Ctrl+V successful plain-text behavior and an empty-provider control.
Record exact input bytes, provider path/order, inserted text including trailing-newline handling, composer state, and whether the draft submits or stays ready.
Add a sanitized provenance observation and machine-validated fixture, update the existing clipboard unknowns and parity matrix, and wire the fixture into the reference verification gate.
Keep this task research-only: do not implement successful clipboard reads or image/path attachment behavior until the reference contract is stable and reviewable.

result.summary: Captured Hermes successful text clipboard parity with a synthetic xclip provider in a direct 120x40 PTY: raw Ctrl+V invokes xclip with -selection clipboard -out, inserts text at the cursor, preserves internal newlines and meaningful spaces, strips trailing newlines, and remains ready without submission. An empty-provider control leaves the draft unchanged; the later image-gateway fallback is explicitly environment-sensitive because no gateway response was attached.

tasks.title: Implement Hermes successful text clipboard parity
acceptance: Add a CLI-owned text clipboard provider following the stable Hermes Linux order: WSL powershell.exe when WSL is detected, wl-paste --type text when Wayland is present, then xclip -selection clipboard -out; provider failures fall through.
Accept only usable text, remove trailing newline runs after a successful read, and preserve internal newlines, meaningful spaces, and cursor insertion semantics.

Wire ready, non-overlay Ctrl+V to InputEvent::Paste without submission or busy state, while retaining the existing no-image fallback for empty or unusable providers and leaving busy/overlay behavior unchanged.

Add focused provider/normalization tests plus a direct 120x40 PTY replay with a synthetic xclip success case and empty control; wire a sanitized Hades fixture into just verify without touching the host clipboard.
Keep image attachments, path paste, OSC52 precedence, and gateway behavior out of scope until their reference contracts are separately observed.

result.summary: Implemented Hermes-compatible native text clipboard parity at the Hades CLI boundary. The provider module follows WSL powershell.exe, Wayland wl-paste --type text, then xclip -selection clipboard -out; command failures fall through, successful empty/unusable output retains the existing image-miss fallback, and usable text preserves internal newlines/meaningful spaces while removing trailing newline runs. Ready non-overlay Ctrl+V becomes a non-submitting paste event; busy and overlay paths do not read the provider. Focused provider/event tests and an isolated 120x40 direct-PTY replay pass synthetic xclip success and empty controls without host clipboard access.
